title: Blind, shuffled and double-scored review
statement: Score compared versions blind to which system or maker produced each, in shuffled order, and have a second person independently score a preset share plus every disputed or severe case.
example: One plan has a second person independently score a preset 25% of the first reviews, 168 of them, plus every disputed or severe case.
detail: An experiment plan hides model identities and response order from the people scoring, and has a second person independently score a preset, stratified 25% of the first reviews (168) plus every disputed or severe case, with differences adjudicated (`uae-education-ai/HERETIC_PLAN.md`). Its harness treats the first-review report as preliminary until those second reviews and the dispute coverage exist (`uae-education-ai/HARNESS.md`). Keep tuning and calibration items out of the final evaluation.
against: The protocol had not been run: no human ratings existed when it was written (`uae-education-ai/REVIEW_PACKET.md`). The protocol has not run: its handover says "The handover is ready; the experiment has not run."

evidence.quote: Blind model IDs and response order.
independently reviews a prespecified, family/condition-stratified 25% of first reviews (**168**, plus every disputed or severe case); adjudicate differences.
Its first-review locked report is explicitly preliminary; an adjudicated report additionally requires the prespecified second reviews and dispute coverage.
Artifact scoring packets use random IDs and balanced assignment. Scorers never see arm, model, prompt, cost, or other scorer labels.
Pilot/development clusters are permanently excluded from final evaluation.
The handover is ready; the experiment has not run.
A human audit rate is a floor, not a target; any automatic/human disagreement expands to the entire predeclared audit block and may stop the phase.

Blind model judging (gemini-3.1-pro-preview and gemini-3.8-flash, two shuffles each, `judging/judgments.json`): all four passes ranked 2.5 Pro takes above every 3.8 take, mainly on exact words and pace.
Constructed-response calibration uses two independent reviewers and a third adjudicator for disagreement.
